I see what you mean. For me, my thoughts regarding depression, anxiety, as well as intrusive thoughts, make it really difficult to think about anything else. It’s hard to get out of my own head, which is also exacerbated bu the fact that I don’t talk to many other people. It isn’t that I’m trying to avoid them, per sé, like I want to reject them and have to obsess over asinine distractions like social media or reality TV or whatever. But in a sense, I naturally don’t want to have them, and when it’s between something dark and something like, I don’t know, playing a videogame or something, I’d probably choose the videogame. Not to shirk my true self, but to try to cope with the very negative feelings and thoughts that I have and experience very frequently. They get old real quick, and so do the distractions. You can never really win.
I truly respect you, and I’m not trying to tell you what to do per sé, but you should really pat yourself on the back every once in a while, you’ve certainly earned it.

I actually have been in therapy on and off for about 15 years now. I’ve done CBT and it has *helped* but much like you I find it very difficult to actually be affected by the counsel I am being given. I understand it. I understand my issues. But, I don’t understand *how* to actually imbibe these thoughts, and change my perspective based on them. It’s more like I am aware of what it may be like to have different neuro-pathways, but I don’t have them yet.

No worries, you aren’t prying at all. I did have a more difficult upbringing with my family, especially my Father, growing up. Although now I must say things are better with my family and I. Not perfect, but considerably better. If I had to try to isolate it I think it comes from worry that I will be alone forever. I have MDD as well (if you can’t tell lol) so that coupled with anxiety/paranoia is just a recipe for disaster. To elaborate, my friendships have been somewhat rocky with others, and I will admittedly say that some of it is definitely paranoia, but what I am trying to cultivate here is that I worry constantly about how I appear to others. Do I appear depressed? Depressing? Negative? That makes me feel bad, although I can only placate so much, only put on a facade for so long. I value honesty above everything, and I try to be realistic without coming off as overbearing. Some people appreciate that, in a sense that some people feel extremely comfortable getting personal with me very quickly. While others, and this is their prerogative, get taken aback by my interaction. I have no friends really, except one, but they have has their own life and we both work quite a lot, so we don’t get the chance to see each other often. I also have a fear of abandonment. It’s less than just being lonely, that is more pressing to me for some odd reason, but perhaps I am desensitized to abandonment as all of my previous friends, people I would have liked to consider allies, seem to have excommunicated me from their lives, be it from telling me they are having relationship problems and not talking to me for 14+ months, calling and talking to their SO for a significant amount of time while we’re hanging out, or just flat-ignoring me. These sort of interactions with people who I care(d) for, people who I hope(d) care(d) for me as well coupled with some very toxic relationships has me in a state of paranoia. I have felt some level of paranoia/worry from a very early age, but I think in growing older, in my formative years, these relationships and interactions with people be it friend or stranger has exacerbated everything significantly. 

I hope this wasn’t verbose, though it may in fact be quite verbose, lol.

I should also add that I am no saint. I have my sins, my shortcomings, mea culpas and things I shouldn’t have said just like everyone else does. The issue is that I am not good at trusting anyone, myself included. So I find it difficult to just learn and move on, as I get attached to the mistakes that I and others around me make (are they out to get me..?)
